prompt: Which of these go into the cache key of a `COPY . .` step? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The layer it is built on
choices.why: Yes: change anything above, and this key changes too.

choices.text: The instruction's text
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The content of the files it copies
choices.why: Yes: one changed byte changes the key.

choices.text: The time of day the build runs
choices.why: Time is not part of any key; an unchanged build at night is fully cached.

prompt: Ana rebuilt with nothing changed and every step said `CACHED`. What did the builder do in those 0.313 seconds?

choices.text: Compiled again, very quickly
choices.why: Nothing compiled; `go build` did not run at all.

choices.text: Downloaded the layers from Docker Hub
choices.why: They were local; `shelf:dev` was never pushed.

choices.text: Checked the keys and reused every layer
choices.why: Right. The image points at layers the builder already had.

choices.text: Copied the previous image byte for byte
choices.why: Nothing is copied; the same layers are reused in place.

prompt: Why was the `RUN go build` layer 146MB when `shelf` is one program?
hint: What else did `go build` write while it ran?

choices.text: The layer holds a copy of the whole Go toolchain
choices.why: The toolchain is in the base image's layers below.

choices.text: Layers are padded to a minimum size
choices.why: The `CMD` layer is 0B; there is no padding.

choices.text: `docker history` counts the size twice
choices.why: The sizes are per layer, counted once.

choices.text: It also holds Go's build cache under `/root/.cache`
choices.why: Right. Everything the step wrote, it keeps.

prompt: Once a step's key changes, that step and every step ___ it are rebuilt.
With `COPY . .` before `go build`, Ana added a README and the build took 19.8 seconds. Why did a file the program never reads cost a full compile?
hint: What does `COPY . .` put into its key?

choices.text: Its checksum entered the `COPY` key, which invalidated the build below
choices.why: Right. The `COPY` changed, so every later step ran.

choices.text: The README is compiled into the binary
choices.why: Go never reads it; it is not a source file.

choices.text: Docker rebuilds everything whenever a new file appears in the project, by design
choices.why: With `COPY *.go` the same README cost nothing.

choices.text: README files are not allowed in images
choices.why: They are allowed; this one simply changed a key.

prompt: With the dependencies-first Dockerfile, how many seconds did the build after the `main.go` edit take? Use the `real` value.
Put the lines of Ana's ordered Dockerfile in order, from top to bottom.
A Python service's Dockerfile has `COPY . .` then `RUN pip install -r requirements.txt`. Which rewrite lets code edits skip the install?

choices.text: Add `--no-cache` to the build
choices.why: That rebuilds everything every time, the opposite.

choices.text: Dependencies first, the code last
choices.why: Right: copy `requirements.txt`, run `pip install`, then copy the code; the install's key depends only on the requirements file.

choices.text: Move `pip install` to the very end of the file
choices.why: Then it runs after every code change, the problem as before.

choices.text: Install with `ADD` instead of `RUN`
choices.why: `ADD` copies files; it cannot install packages.

prompt: In the ordered Dockerfile, why did the README change leave every step `CACHED`?

choices.text: The README was listed in `.dockerignore`
choices.why: It was not; the ignore file lists `.git`, `.env`, `testdata/` and the Dockerfiles.

choices.text: The builder skips files whose names are in capitals
choices.why: Names do not matter; what is copied does.

choices.text: `COPY *.go ./` only copies Go files
choices.why: Right, so the README changes no key.

choices.text: The cache always ignores Markdown files
choices.why: `COPY . .` did copy it and paid for it.

prompt: What does `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build go build …` keep between builds?

choices.text: The compiled binary, inside the image
choices.why: The binary is in the layer as always; the mount is separate.

choices.text: The whole layer, so the step never runs again
choices.why: The step did run again, in 0.9 seconds.

choices.text: Nothing; mounts are discarded after each step
choices.why: A cache mount is kept by the builder, unlike a tmpfs.

choices.text: Go's build cache, kept outside any layer
choices.why: Right. The step still runs, but finds the compiled packages.

prompt: A Dockerfile has `RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl`, unchanged for a year. On the same machine, what does a normal `docker build` give you today?
hint: What does that step's key contain?

choices.text: The year-old layer, reused, with its year-old packages
choices.why: Right. Use `--no-cache` or `--pull` when the point is to get updates.

choices.text: Today's package list, because `apt-get update` always runs
choices.why: It only runs if its key changed, and nothing in the key did.

choices.text: An error, because cached package lists expire
choices.why: The cache has no expiry; it trusts its keys.

choices.text: A fresh install, because `-y` disables the cache
choices.why: `-y` answers apt's questions; it has nothing to do with Docker's cache.

prompt: Match each option or command to what it does.
hint: Two are about the cache, one about the base image, one about disk.

pairs.right: Ignores every cached layer for this build
Fetches the newest base image first
Reports how much disk the build cache uses

right_distractors: Deletes every image on the machine

prompt: Ana's team changes a dependency version once a month and code all day. Which combination fits best?
hint: One technique for each kind of change.

choices.text: `COPY . .` first, plus `--no-cache` on every build
choices.why: That pays for everything every time.

choices.text: Order plus a cache mount
choices.why: Right: dependencies first, and a cache mount for the package manager; ordering saves code edits; the mount saves most of a dependency change.

choices.text: Only `--pull`, so the base image is always fresh
choices.why: That changes when the base updates, not how edits are cached.

choices.text: A single `RUN` doing everything, so there is one layer
choices.why: One layer means any change rebuilds all of it.

prompt: Why is the first build on a fresh CI runner slow even with a well-ordered Dockerfile?
hint: What does the runner start with?

choices.text: CI runners have slower processors
choices.why: Perhaps, but the cause here is what is missing.

choices.text: Dockerfiles are ignored on CI
choices.why: They are used exactly as on a laptop.

choices.text: Its build cache is empty
choices.why: Right. Lesson 26 stores the cache in a registry to fix that.

choices.text: BuildKit is disabled on CI
choices.why: It is the default builder there too.
